group: CollectorContext.add(String, Collector<E>) - basic functionality and edge cases

cases.expected: CollectorContext.get("testCollector") returns the same SimpleCollector instance that was added
cases.description: Verify that a normal collector can be added and retrieved using the same name.

cases.expected: CollectorContext.get(null) returns the SimpleCollector instance (HashMap permits null keys)
cases.description: Check behaviour when the name argument is null – the map should store the entry under a null key without throwing.
Validate that adding a null collector stores a null value for the given name.

cases.expected: After first add, get("duplicate") returns the first collector; after second add with a different collector, get("duplicate") returns the second collector
cases.description: Ensure that adding a collector with an existing name overwrites the previous entry.

cases.expected: CollectorContext.getAll().size() == 2 and each name maps to its respective collector
cases.description: Add two distinct collectors and verify that both are present and the map size reflects the number of distinct keys.
Confirm that the generic type parameter does not affect the storage – a Collector<String> can be stored and retrieved.
Same as previous test but with a different generic type to prove type‑erasure handling.

group: CollectorContext.add(String, Collector<E>) - additional edge cases and robustness

cases.expected: CollectorContext.get("") returns the SimpleCollector instance that was added
cases.description: Verify that an empty string is a valid key and can be used to store and retrieve a collector.

cases.expected: CollectorContext.get("   ") returns the SimpleCollector instance that was added
cases.description: Check that a name consisting only of whitespace characters is accepted as a map key.
Ensure that special characters in the name do not affect storage/retrieval.

cases.expected: CollectorContext.get(veryLongName) returns the SimpleCollector instance without throwing any exception
cases.description: Stress test with a very long (5,000‑character) name to confirm the method handles large keys gracefully.

cases.expected: CollectorContext.get("subCollector") returns the same CustomCollector instance
cases.description: Validate that a collector of a subclass type (CustomCollector extends SimpleCollector) is stored and retrieved correctly.

cases.expected: After adding null, CollectorContext.get("nullThenReal") returns null; after a second add with a non‑null collector, get returns the new collector and getAll().size() remains 1
cases.description: Test overwriting a previously stored null value with a real collector; map size should not increase.

cases.expected: After adding the same collector instance a second time with the same name, CollectorContext.get("sameInstance") still returns that instance and getAll().size() stays 1
cases.description: Confirm that adding the identical instance under an existing key does not change the map size or the stored reference.

cases.expected: CollectorContext.get("ユニコード") returns the SimpleCollector instance
cases.description: Check that Unicode characters in the name are handled correctly.

cases.expected: After a second add with name = new String("duplicateKey") and collector = new SimpleCollector<>("second"), CollectorContext.get("duplicateKey") returns the second collector and getAll().size() remains 1
cases.description: Verify that map key equality is based on String.equals, not object identity; a different String object with the same content overwrites the previous entry.
